PullRequest.Title: Agents window: open the extension's page from Manage Extension
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #325141

## Problem

In the Agents window, an extension's notification offers **Manage Extension** in its gear menu, and the same item appears in extension progress notifications and the status bar context menu. Clicking it fails with "command '_extensions.manage' not found", because the Agents window never registered that command.

## Change

- The Agents window now always registers `_extensions.manage`, so callers can always invoke it.
- The command opens the extension's page in the Extensions section of Agent Customizations when it can.
- When it can't, because the Agents window doesn't manage extensions, it shows an info notification: "Extension '{0}' can't be managed in this window right now."
- The command ID is shared as one constant, `MANAGE_EXTENSION_COMMAND_ID`, used by every place that runs or registers it.

## Demo

Before, on Insiders 1.147.0: Manage Extension fails with "command '_extensions.manage' not found".

After, when Agents-window extension management is on: Manage Extension opens the extension's page.

After, when it is off: Manage Extension says the extension can't be managed in this window right now.

## How tested

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/test/browser/agentsWindowExtensionManageCommand.test.ts` (plus the related extension, notification and progress suites): passed, 22 tests
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- UI scenario on the dev build, macOS arm64, Agents window, with a test extension that shows an error notification. Opening the notification center, then gear → Manage Extension:
  - management on: the extension's page opens (passed)
  - management off: the "can't be managed" notification appears (passed)
  - installed Insiders: "command '_extensions.manage' not found" (the bug)

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup and extensions contribution registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extensions contribution module evaluates during Agents-window startup and synchronously registers one command handler. The handler's service lookups, configuration read, and editor work do not run until invocation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per window: one command registration. The added handler module statically references the customization editor, but that editor was already in this contribution's startup graph through AgentsWindowExtensionsAccessibilityHelp, so the diff does not add that heavyweight module to startup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer startup sequence; no queue, limiter, or asynchronous work is introduced by command registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted or populated by the registration. Existing module loading remains one-time and module-cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the contribution imports and existing accessibility-help dependency that startup gains only constant registration work, not new editor construction or I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Module-graph byte-level effects were not measured, but the direct heavyweight dependency was already transitively loaded before the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the registration is constant-time and does not move editor, filesystem, IPC, or network work onto startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Manage Extension while Agents-window extension management is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A notification, progress item, or status-bar action dispatches the in-process command; the handler reads one configuration value and synchronously enqueues an informational notification.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One command dispatch and one notification per explicit user invocation; independent of installed-extension count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-driven invocations execute independently with no introduced fan-out; normal menu interaction makes aggregate concurrency effectively one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration service supplies its existing in-memory value; no new cache or negative-cache state is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete handler branch and unchanged action call sites apart from the shared command constant.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Notification rendering cost is platform-dependent but constant and existing infrastructure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance issue: the disabled branch is bounded constant work and has no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Manage Extension for an installed extension with management enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command opens or reuses the Agent Customizations editor, selects the Extensions section, then finds the requested extension and starts its detail page. On a cold editor, section construction synchronously groups and sorts installed extensions and updates the virtual tree before the detail page is selected; this scales with installed extensions, but it is existing section initialization and realistic counts do not establish a concrete regression severe enough to report. The extension detail loader may fetch its manifest, but showExtension starts that promise without awaiting it in the command handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected extension's manifest through the existing ExtensionEditor detail-page loader; readme and changelog remain lazy until their tabs consume them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one manifest resolution for the explicitly selected extension per page render; no installed-extension fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: In the Agents window the command was unregistered and failed, so this detail boundary was unreachable from Manage Extension; users could already incur the same one-extension boundary by opening the Extensions section and selecting an extension manually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The detail renderer awaits the manifest before completing its full render, but manageExtension does not await page.show; editor opening and in-memory section initialization are the synchronous command critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold section initialization is O(N log N) in the number of installed non-built-in extensions; lookup is O(N). Detail loading has effective cardinality one requested extension, not one boundary per installed extension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One editor-open operation followed by one detail load per invocation. There is no loop issuing boundary calls and no Promise.all burst. Rapid independent user invocations are not coalesced, but the trigger is a menu action rather than a high-frequency path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The editor input is singleton/reused when warm; the section widget and extension page are reused while the editor remains open. ExtensionEditor wraps readme, changelog, and manifest access in per-render lazy caches; only manifest is requested eagerly for the selected detail. Empty marketplace search performs no network query.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced call path, O(N log N) cold in-memory work, single selected-extension boundary, and lack of boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold in-memory list initialization can grow for unusually large extension sets, but the tree is virtualized and no benchmark or code evidence establishes material user-visible delay at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new feature reaches one existing detail load and existing cold section initialization; it does not add per-extension I/O, concurrency bursts, unbounded retention, or repeated hot-path work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Manage Extension for an extension that is not installed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command opens the Extensions section, performs one in-memory scan of local extensions, then assigns the identifier to the existing search input when no local match exists.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One O(N) local lookup over installed extensions per explicit invocation; no loop over search results is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single user-driven command; no background fan-out or limiter interaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm editor/section instances are reused. The marketplace search component cancels superseded requests and does not query for an empty string; the changed handler itself introduces no cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed handler itself performs only editor opening and a local scan before delegating to existing search UI.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether programmatic input assignment subsequently emits the existing search event is a functional detail, not needed to establish performance; no changed code directly issues a network request in this branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the changed code has bounded local work and does not directly create network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manage Extension actions in normal editor windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Notification, progress, and status-bar actions execute the same command implementation as before; only the hard-coded identifier was replaced with a shared constant, and the existing editor-window registration uses that same constant.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One unchanged command dispatch per user action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged extension-service lookup and editor caching behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the diffs that runtime behavior and call cardinality are unchanged in editor windows.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the relevant changed lines are identifier substitutions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: these changes preserve the existing command target and execution cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files and traced startup, disabled-command, installed-extension, missing-extension, and normal-editor scenarios. The PR adds only constant startup registration and user-driven access to existing editor/detail flows. Cold section initialization performs collection-wide in-memory work, but the diff introduces no realistic hot-path fan-out, unbounded retention, cache-lifecycle failure, or expensive boundary burst warranting a finding.
